newsitem.title: UK: Ofgas says to allow Centrica discounts.
newsitem.headline: Ofgas says to allow Centrica discounts.

text.p: Britain's gas regulator Ofgas said on Wednesday that it would allow Centrica Plc's British Gas Home Energy arm to offer discounts to customers in the south-west of England "for now".
But in a statement, Ofgas said the decision should not be
In March, Centrica offered customers in the region who paid bills by direct debit a discount averaging five percent to dissuade them from switching to rival gas suppliers.
The south-west has been used as a test-bed for the introduction of gas competition throughout Britain.

Ofgas is to publish a document on the scheme, known as ValuePlus, later on Wednesday. It said it would seek a change in the company's licence obliging it to inform the regulator three months in advance of any price changes.
"This would ensure that predatory or pre-emptive price cutting does not occur," Ofgas said.

The authority added that it was concerned that actions by Centrica could impede "the development of effective competition throughout Great Britain....and will look particularly closely at any additional proposals to apply selective price cuts."
